RW01V3.title: GitHub · October 2018 MySQL failover
RW01V3.alert: At 22:52 UTC on October 21, a major developer platform began showing stale metadata after an inter-region connectivity event. Background job processing was disrupted; Git repository data access appeared largely intact. Investigate what failed and the recovery tradeoffs in this reconstruction.
observations: Metadata-related pages showed stale or inconsistent information
Some asynchronous jobs stopped progressing
Git repository data was still accessible through independent paths
hypotheses: MySQL failover divergence together with deliberate background-job pause
A universal Git repository storage outage
documented_facts: A network partition triggered MySQL Orchestrator leader changes and West Coast failover.
Divergent writes made immediately failing back unsafe.
GitHub paused webhook delivery and Pages builds to prioritize data integrity.
Recovery involved rebuilding replication topologies and restoring replicas.
model_assumptions: 12 illustrative service nodes, dependency edges, initial unavailability inventory and alert proxies
Boolean state of replication topology and protective job pause
Four hypothetical repair choices with synthetic cost units

RW02V3.title: Cloudflare · June 2022 routing outage
RW02V3.alert: At 06:27 UTC on June 21, a global edge network began failing requests in a subset of locations after an infrastructure rollout. Other regions continued to serve traffic. Inspect the reconstructed network to identify the controlling fault.
observations: A subset of high-traffic locations lost external reachability
Other data centers remained available
The outage coincided with an infrastructure change
hypotheses: An attack on all global locations
Incorrect route announcement policy in the affected MCP network
documented_facts: A routing policy configuration change took 19 Cloudflare data centers offline.
The incident affected approximately half of HTTP requests despite 19 centers representing about 4% of locations.
The team rolled back the incorrect route advertisement policy and restored all affected locations by 07:42 UTC.
model_assumptions: Illustrative three-group representation of 19 sites and 10 service nodes
Boolean router policy and capacity flags
Simulated mitigation candidates, costs, and aggregate health outcomes

RW03V3.title: Cloudflare · July 2019 WAF regex outage
RW03V3.alert: At 13:42 UTC on July 2, edge HTTP requests began returning errors around the time of a security-system deployment. Serving-process CPU rose sharply while DNS remained available. Investigate the reconstruction for a cause and safe repair.
observations: HTTP traffic generated 502 responses
Serving-process CPU saturation was visible
An update to a security component was underway
hypotheses: An external DDoS attack saturated bandwidth
WAF regex backtracking exhausted CPU following a rule deployment
Only a CDN cache invalidation problem
documented_facts: A WAF managed-rule deployment contained a pathological regular expression.
Excessive regex backtracking exhausted CPU on HTTP/HTTPS serving processes.
Users received HTTP 502 errors; rollback of the offending rule restored operation.
model_assumptions: 10 simplified modeled components and dependency relationships
Boolean WAF rule and a hypothetical separate safe-guard switch
Simulation-only candidate repair costs and service availability snapshots

RW04V4.title: Cloudflare · July 2020 backbone routing incident
RW04V4.alert: A backbone configuration change directed traffic into an overloaded routing location. Some regions failed while independent edge locations continued serving. Investigate the modeled route-control failure and redundant paths.
observations: The incident followed a network configuration update
Traffic concentrated around a backbone location
Non-backbone edge paths remained usable
hypotheses: An entire global DNS authority outage
Backbone route attraction overwhelmed one routing hub
documented_facts: A router configuration error attracted excessive traffic to Atlanta on July 17, 2020.
The backbone outage affected only certain locations, and independent edge locations continued serving.
Disabling the affected router restored traffic flow.
model_assumptions: 10 simplified service nodes including one redundantly fed ingress
Synthetic backbone route-attraction and isolation flags
Four hypothetical atomic interventions and cost units

RW05V4.title: Cloudflare · November 2023 control-plane outage
RW05V4.alert: A power incident affected a primary site hosting the control plane and analytics systems. Redundant facilities were not immediately serving all control services. Investigate the modeled multi-dependency failure and recovery.
observations: Control-plane and analytics services degraded
Independent edge request processing continued
A recovery facility was activated during the incident
hypotheses: A malicious application deployment corrupting API handlers
Primary-site power loss and incomplete failover readiness affecting distinct control-plane components
Only a cache TTL configuration error
documented_facts: A power failure at an upstream colocation facility disrupted Cloudflare control-plane and analytics systems in November 2023.
A disaster recovery facility restored most control-plane functionality before all services returned.
The edge network continued routing customer traffic during much of the incident.
model_assumptions: Synthetic Boolean primary-site power and DR availability switches
10 illustrative nodes with independent control and analytics failure paths
Hypothetical atomic repair candidates and costs; not claimed historical actions

RW06V4.title: Cloudflare · June 2025 Workers KV dependency outage
RW06V4.alert: An upstream backing-store failure made key-value lookups unreliable, degrading multiple dependent products. A tempting broad fail-open option risks a previously healthy security control. Identify the minimum complete SAFE intervention in this modeled sandbox.
observations: Multiple products depended on a common key-value service
Uncached key lookups failed while some cached requests succeeded
Core DNS, WAF and proxy paths were not directly affected
hypotheses: A shared backing-storage dependency failure impacting Workers KV consumers
Global BGP hijack of authoritative DNS
A hardware failure of all edge caching nodes
documented_facts: Workers KV relied in part on storage provided by a third party, which experienced an outage on June 12, 2025.
Workers KV failure affected multiple dependent Cloudflare products.
DNS, core proxy, cache and WAF were not directly affected by the incident.
model_assumptions: 10 synthetic service nodes and simplified dependency edges
A deliberately unsafe cheap fail-open alternative affecting an initially healthy service
Hypothetical storage failover, recovery costs and counterfactual effects
